BENCHMARKS

One reproducible comparison suite.

Full methodology

Compare onino v0.4.1, mkp224o, Onionloom and Prefix32 on the same hardware, using unmodified official release binaries and normal key saving.

Measurements and test conditions

At least five runs per configuration, rotating execution order, with at least 15 seconds of actual search warmup and approximately 20-second measurement windows. Candidate-counter deltas use external wall time; startup and autotuning are excluded. Run bun bench/run.mjs to reproduce the suite and regenerate the published results.

Onionloom's GPU-focused configuration includes one CPU search worker; CPU+GPU uses all workers. Onino GPU-only has no CPU search workers. Prefix32's GPU mode uses CPU assistance without independent CPU search. Prefix32 CPU stops on its first match, so shorter searches are not published as sustained comparisons. Its fixed-workload --bench results are not substituted.

The README includes shorter and multi-prefix workloads. The consolidated dataset records all attempts, exact versions and hashes, hardware, build settings, selected modes, counter precision and any exits or unavailable capabilities.

All backends, ranges and test conditions
Million candidates/s . median [min-max]
Machine onino backend onino onionloom Ratio
Debian server Auto / BMI2 + ADX 10.5 [10.4-10.6] 9.04 [8.73-9.05] 1.16x
Ubuntu VPS Auto / BMI2 8.19 [7.99-8.35] 7.05 [6.87-7.15] 1.16x
Ubuntu VPS Forced / BMI2 + ADX 8.49 [8.40-8.60] 7.05 [6.87-7.15] 1.20x
CachyOS laptop Auto / AVX-512 IFMA 45.5 [45.5-45.5] 12.13 [11.89-12.16] 3.75x
CachyOS laptop Forced / BMI2 + ADX 16.5 [16.5-16.6] 12.13 [11.89-12.16] 1.36x

Each configuration ran once for one minute after a 20-second warm-up, pinned to logical CPU 0, with no matches found. The laptop was plugged in with the performance power profile. Ratios compare medians of the printed rates; the tools use different averaging windows. The same onionloom run supplies both backend comparisons on the VPS and laptop.

The Xeon server has BMI2 and ADX, without AVX-512. The VPS reports a Haswell guest CPU with BMI2 but no ADX; automatic selection used BMI2. The separate forced BMI2 + ADX run executed successfully despite that feature report. The guest model does not identify the underlying physical processor. The Ryzen laptop supports AVX-512 IFMA.

These project measurements include 148 progress samples across eight runs. Binary versions and build commands were not recorded for the Linux runs.

GET STARTED

Run onino.

Download a release
01 /

Install

Linux / macOS
sh 
curl -fsSL https://src.ws2.sh/onino/install.sh | sh

Choose CPU or GPU when prompted. The installer verifies the release checksum.

Windows binaries and other downloads
02 /

Start searching

onino --cpu all 'hello.'

Find addresses beginning with hello using all CPU workers. Matches are saved under matches/.

Search continues until you press Ctrl+C.

EVERY SAVED MATCH
hostnamehs_ed25519_public_keyhs_ed25519_secret_key

PATTERN SYNTAX

Search patterns.

Match a prefix, a suffix or text in between. Pass multiple patterns to search for any of them.

Full matcher reference
Supported CPU search patterns
Pattern Matches
hello. Starts with hello
.hello Ends with hello
hello.world Starts with hello, ends with world
.hello. Contains hello strictly inside
hello Contains hello anywhere

Patterns use a-z and 2-7 and match the first 52 hostname characters. Suffixes end at character 52, before the last four characters. GPU search accepts 1-8 literal prefixes only.
